source.author: ov
source.text: ardua iamdudum resonat tinnitibus Ide, tutus ut infanti vagiat ore puer.
source.text_original: ardua iamdudum resonat tinnitibus Ide, / tutus ut infanti vagiat ore puer.
source.text_english: Already for some time high Ida resounds with clashing sounds, as when a child cries safely from an infant mouth.

reuse.author: lact
reuse.text: sed et matris eius mysterium idem continet; quod Ouidius exponit in Fastis: ardua iam dudum resonat tinnitibus Ide, tutus ut infanti uagiat ore puer.
reuse.text_original: sed et matris eius mysterium idem continet; quod Ouidius exponit in Fastis: ardua iam dudum resonat tinnitibus Ide, tutus ut infanti uagiat ore puer.
reuse.text_english: But the mystery of his mother too contains the same thing, which Ovid explains in the Fasti: lofty Ida has long been resounding with clashing sounds, so that the child may wail safely in the infant’s mouth.
